concept.title: Privacy and safety
concept.shortdesc: shares your profile in stages. Knowing what each stage shares helps you choose what your card shows.

fig.title: What other phones see at each stage

image.alt: Three stages. Broadcast: age band, some interests, and a rotating ID. Connected: name, age, line, interests, photo, newest public post and story. Matched: chat, calls, notes, stories and posts.

section.title: Before any connection
section.p: While Nearby is on, your phone sends out a small signal that phones near you or on the same Wi-Fi can read, even if they don't have . It holds only your age band, some of your interests, and a random ID that changes every 15 minutes. It never holds your name or photo.

The signal is a Multipeer Connectivity advertisement of at most 24 bytes: the rotating ID, the age band, three flags (open to a hi, photo available, and a relay flag that is always off), and a subset of interests. With one or two interests, all are included; otherwise 60% rounded up, at most six, reshuffled each time the ID changes. The ID does not rotate while a connection is open. See .

section.title: When phones connect
section.p: phones close by connect on their own, before either of you taps Say hi. Once connected, they can see:

ul.li: Your first name and your age, or your age band if you turn off Show my age.
Your one line about yourself and all your interests.
Your photo, when Who can see your photo is set to Everyone nearby. This is the default.
Your newest post and story shared with everyone nearby.

section.p: Your date of birth never leaves your phone.
section.note: To share less before you match, turn off Show my age and set Who can see your photo to After we match. See .

section.title: After you match
section.p: When you both say hi, you can chat, call, and leave notes, and you see each other's stories and posts.
